cls: Antineoplastic - non-covalent (reversible) Bruton tyrosine kinase (BTK) inhibitor
pharm: Reversible non-covalent BTK inhibitor; inhibits both wild-type and C481-mutant BTK that resists covalent BTK inhibitors
quick: Can cause fetal harm; verify status; effective contraception during and after treatment per labeling
Do not breastfeed during treatment and after last dose per labeling
See full labeling; monitor renal function with diarrhoea/vomiting/dehydration risk
See full labeling; dose-reduce in moderate-severe impairment for hepatically cleared agents
No specific interaction; avoid excess with hepatotoxic or myelosuppressive therapy
CBC, LFTs, drug-specific toxicities, pregnancy status
summary: Pirtobrutinib (Jaypirca) is a non-covalent BTK inhibitor for relapsed or refractory mantle cell lymphoma after 2+ lines including a covalent BTK inhibitor, and for CLL/SLL after covalent BTK inhibitor and BCL2 inhibitor exposure. Reversible binding overcomes C481 resistance mutations. Key risks are bleeding, infections (including opportunistic), cytopenias, atrial arrhythmias and second primary malignancies.
indications: Relapsed or refractory mantle cell lymphoma after at least 2 lines including a BTK inhibitor
Relapsed or refractory chronic lymphocytic leukaemia / small lymphocytic lymphoma after a BTK inhibitor and a BCL2 inhibitor

dosage.d: 200 mg once daily continuously until progression or unacceptable toxicity
dosage.t: With or without food; swallow whole
dosage.n: Reduce to 100 mg daily (or 50 mg) with severe renal impairment or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors; hold peri-operatively for bleeding risk

admin: Take exactly as prescribed; do not crush, split or chew unless labeling allows
Take at the same time(s) each day; if a dose is missed follow the missed-dose rule - do not double
Report interacting new medicines including antifungals, anti-TB drugs, antiepileptics and St John's wort (CYP3A4)
Store in the original container with desiccant where supplied; protect from moisture
moa: Pirtobrutinib is a reversible, non-covalent BTK inhibitor that binds BTK without requiring the C481 residue, so it inhibits both wild-type BTK and C481-mutant BTK that drives resistance to covalent BTK inhibitors, blocking B-cell-receptor survival signalling.

relative: Bleeding diathesis or anticoagulant/antiplatelet use (hold before surgery)
Active infection (treat first; prophylaxis per risk)

preg: No adequate human data. Based on mechanism, fetal harm is expected. Verify pregnancy status before starting; advise effective contraception during treatment and for the specified period after the last dose. Use in pregnancy only if the potential benefit justifies the potential fetal risk.
lact: No data on presence in human milk. Because of potential serious adverse reactions in the breastfed infant, advise women not to breastfeed during treatment and for the specified period after the last dose.
renal: Mild-moderate impairment: no routine change unless labeled; severe: limited data - monitor for exaggerated toxicity and dehydration-related AKI.
hepatic: Mild impairment: monitor; moderate-severe: dose-reduce or avoid per labeling (most agents hepatically cleared).

major: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (raise exposure - reduce pirtobrutinib dose)
moderate: Anticoagulants and antiplatelets (additive bleeding - monitor closely)
interactions.alcohol: Avoid excess alcohol with hepatotoxic therapy.
interactions.diagnostics: No characteristic laboratory test interference; monitor disease-specific markers.

serious: Serious infections including pneumonia and opportunistic infections
emergency: Uncontrolled bleeding or black stools/vomited blood - seek emergency care
Fever with neutropenia, or severe breathlessness (infection) - seek urgent care
Palpitations with dizziness/fainting (arrhythmia) - seek emergency care

counsel: Bruising and bleeding are common - report nosebleeds, blood in urine/stool, or unusual bruises; tell surgeons/dentists you take it
Report fever, cough or breathlessness promptly (infection risk)
Report fast or irregular heartbeat, dizziness or fainting
Attend skin checks; use sun protection; use contraception
pk: Target inhibition within hours-days; response assessed in weeks
Room temperature 20-25 C in original container; protect from moisture
pearls: Non-covalent design specifically addresses C481-mutant resistance to ibrutinib/acalabrutinib/zanubrutinib
Hold before and after surgery (3-7 days per bleeding risk) like other BTK inhibitors
Dose-reduce rather than stop for strong CYP3A4 inhibitor co-therapy
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as remembered on the same day unless it is near the next dose; never double up. Take as soon as remembered on the same day; do not double.
overdose: No specific antidote. Withhold drug and give supportive care with monitoring of CBC, ECG, LFTs and agent-specific toxicities. Contact Poison Help (1-800-222-1222).
